sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150064
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 24755 of 2024

Applicant :- Anil Kumar Sharma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Kartikeya Saran,Vineet Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vishal Mohan Gupta
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Short counter affidavit filed on behalf of informant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Kartikeya Saran and Vineet Kumar Singh, learned counsels for the applicant, Sri Vishal Mohan Gupta and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
218 of 2017, under Sections 406, 420, 506, 452 IPC, Police Station- Surajpur, District- Gautam Buddh Nagar, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that however, FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2017 but applicant is not an absconder and during investigation, he was not arrested by the Investigating Officer as all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class with maximum punishment of seven years.

Anil Kumar Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15953887/

sentences.text: He further submitted that however, charge sheet was filed in the year 2018 but unfortunately no summons could ever be served upon the applicant.

He further submitted that when applicant came to know that coercive measures are being taken against him then he approached before this Court and filed anticipatory bail application and on the direction given by this Court, he appeared before the court concerned and thereafter he was sent to jail.

6. He further submitted that as far as merit of the present case is concerned, as per allegation,
applicant has taken loan of Rs. 37 lakhs from the informant but failed to repay the loan and thereafter he executed an agreement to sell in favour of the informant but in spite of that he did not execute the sale deed.

7. He further submitted that present dispute attracts only civil liability and in fact, informant of the case also filed a civil declaratory suit and after the order passed by court concerned, sale deed of the property in question has been executed in favour of the informant.

8. He further submitted that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 04.06.2024.
9.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is an absconder and after the process under Sections 82/83 Cr.P.C., he could only be appeared before the court concerned but could not dispute the other arguments on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, it reflects that FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2017 and after investigation, charge sheet was filed against the applicant in the year 2018 and it also reflects from the record that after the process under Sections 82/83 Cr.P.C. applicant appeared before the court concerned but it appears that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class with maximum punishment of seven years and during investigation, applicant was not arrested and at the time of charge sheet, which has been annexed along with the instant bail application, the Investigating Officer did not state that applicant is an absconder.

12. Futher, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that however, summons were issued against the applicant but the same could never be served upon him, cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.

13. Further, as far as merit of the present case is concerned, present dispute appears to be civil dispute and with regard to property in question, informant also filed a civil declaratory suit and pursuant to the order passed by the competent civil court, sale deed of the property in question has already been executed in favour of the informant.

sentences.text: Further, law is settled, bail is a rule and bail rejection is an exception and bail cannot be withheld for punitive purpose.
15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
16. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant- Anil Kumar Sharma be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

19. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
